subject: Archaeology
title: How Sites Are Discovered
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on How Sites Are Discovered.

hook.text: Most archaeological sites are found by accident — farmers plowing fields, builders digging foundations.

buildup.text: The Terracotta Army was found by farmers digging a well. Lascaux Cave was found by teenagers chasing a runaway dog.

discovery.text: Professional surveys also find sites. Archaeologists walk fields in lines, scanning the ground for pottery and flint.

twist.text: Construction projects destroy more sites than they reveal. Most countries require surveys before building.

climax.text: Satellite imagery and LiDAR now find hidden sites from space. Thousands of unknown ruins have been spotted from above.

punchline.text: A dog, a well, a satellite — archaeology starts with someone noticing something.

quiz.question: How are most archaeological sites initially discovered?
options: By professional archaeologists conducting planned excavations
By accident — farmers, builders, or people stumbling on remains
By satellite imagery scanning from orbit

details.summary: Archaeological sites are discovered through farmer field-walking, construction projects, erosion, metal detecting, aerial photography, satellite imagery, LiDAR, geophysical survey, and sometimes pure accident. Many of the greatest discoveries — Lascaux, the Terracotta Army — were found by chance.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding how sites are found reveals that discovery depends heavily on where archaeologists look and what technologies they use. New survey methods continuously reveal sites invisible to previous generations of researchers.
takeaways: Sites are found through survey, accident, erosion, and construction
New technologies like LiDAR reveal previously invisible sites
Many famous discoveries were completely accidental

faq.question: What percentage of archaeological sites have been discovered?
faq.answer: Estimates suggest only a tiny fraction — perhaps 1-5% — of sites worldwide have been identified. Tropical forests, ocean floors, deep cave systems, and built-up urban areas conceal countless undiscovered sites. Every new technology reveals more of what has been missed.

faq.question: How do construction projects lead to archaeological discoveries?
faq.answer: Plowing, foundation digging, road building, and pipeline trenching expose buried deposits. Legal requirements for pre-construction archaeological assessment in many countries ensure that discoveries are documented. Without these laws, most construction-revealed sites would be destroyed unrecorded.
